content: Cefprozil is a semi-synthetic antibiotic that belongs to the cephalosporin class and has a broad spectrum of activity. It exists as a mixture of cis and trans isomers, with the cis isomer comprising at least 90% of the mixture. The chemical name of cefprozil monohydrate is (6R, 7R)-7-[[(2Z)-2-(2-amino-4-thiazolyl)-2-(methoxyimino)acetyl]amino]-8-oxo-3-propenyl-5-thia-1-azabicyclo[4.2.0]oct-2-ene-2-carboxylic acid monohydrate. Its structural formula reflects this composition. Cefprozil appears as a white to yellowish powder. The molecular formula of the monohydrate form is C18H19N3O5S·H2O, and its molecular weight is 407.44 g/mol. Each cefprozil tablet, designed for oral use, contains an amount of cefprozil equivalent to either 250 mg or 500 mg of anhydrous cefprozil. The tablets also include several inactive ingredients, such as hypromellose, magnesium stearate, methylcellulose, microcrystalline cellulose, polyethylene glycol 400, polysorbate 80, sodium starch glycolate, and titanium dioxide. Additionally, the 500 mg tablets contain ferric oxide. Cefprozil is also available as an oral suspension, which is intended for oral administration. The oral suspension contains cefprozil in amounts equivalent to either 125 mg or 250 mg of anhydrous cefprozil per 5 mL of the reconstituted liquid. The suspension formulation includes the following inactive ingredients: aspartame, carboxymethylcellulose sodium, anhydrous citric acid, colloidal silicon dioxide, FD&C Yellow No. 6, glycine, a combination of microcrystalline cellulose and carboxymethylcellulose sodium, polysorbate 80, simethicone, sodium benzoate, sodium chloride, sucrose, and a Tutti-Frutti flavoring agent.
